hints: Focus on what electron capture does to the nucleus, a proton is lost but the total mass number stays the same.
Germanium has proton number 32, so losing one proton gives the new element proton number 31 with mass number still 68.
Use neutrons = nucleon number minus proton number for the new atom to check its composition.
walkthrough:
**Understand the nuclear change**

Think of this as a proton swallowing an electron inside the nucleus. One proton becomes one neutron.

$$p + e^- \rightarrow n$$

**Find the new proton number**

Germanium, $\text{Ge}$, has proton number $Z = 32$. Losing one proton means the new element X has one fewer proton.

$$Z(X) = 32 - 1 = 31$$

**Find the neutrons in $^{68}$X**

The nucleon (mass) number stays at 68 because one proton is replaced by one neutron. Neutrons = mass number minus proton number.

$$\text{neutrons} = 68 - 31 = 37$$

**Identify X and check electrons**

Proton number 31 is gallium, $\text{Ga}$, so $^{68}$X is $^{68}\text{Ga}$. A neutral atom has 31 electrons with configuration $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{10}4s^24p^1$, which confirms the neutron count is the correct statement.

options.A: Incorrect. X is gallium with $Z = 31$ and configuration $[Ar] 3d^{10}4s^24p^1$, so it has only 1 electron in its outer p orbitals, not 4. The value 4 would fit Group 14 like Ge itself.
options.B: Incorrect. The outer (n=4) shell of Ga is $4s^24p^1$, which is only 3 electrons, not 13. The number 13 comes from wrongly adding the $3d^{10}$ electrons to the outer shell.
options.C: Correct. Mass number remains 68 while proton number falls from 32 to 31, so neutrons = 68 - 31 = 37. This is exactly what electron capture does, proton down by one, neutron up by one.
options.D: Incorrect. 32 is the proton number of the starting $^{68}\text{Ge}$. Since one proton changed into a neutron, X must have proton number 31, not 32.
